text:
Eric Huang: Quick ask — can someone run a focused quant comparison for mpt-30b? I want concrete latency / cost / quality numbers for int8 vs int4 vs fp8. Suspect int4 gives latency wins but might drop on long-context "hot" prompts. Target batch sizes: 1, 8, 32. Please include KV cache on/off. pinging @Cheng Li and @perf-bot :pray:

Maria Lopez: Clarifying q — which eval sets do you want? devbench long-context, or our hot-prompts set? Also do we want sampling fixed (top_p/top_k) or generation config left default?

Eric Huang: Hot-prompts + devbench long-context subset. Use fixed sampling: top_p=0.95, temp=0.0 for determinism. Label runs with kv_on / kv_off.

Cheng Li: Got it. I'll schedule perf-bot runs. Adding a small human-eval style prompt subset to catch hallucination spikes. Command I'll use:
```
perf-bot schedule run 
  --job qcmp-17721 
  --model mpt-30b 
  --quant int8,int4,fp8 
  --batch-sizes 1,8,32 
  --kv-cfg on,off 
  --eval-sets hot-prompts,devbench-long,human-eval-sample 
  --gen top_p=0.95,temp=0.0 
  --metrics p50,p95,token-cost,acc-hotprompts,perplexity 
  --output /tmp/qcmp-17721.json
```

perf-bot: Job scheduled: id=qcmp-17721, ETA ~45m. configs: models=mpt-30b.quant(int8,int4,fp8); batch=[1,8,32]; kv=[on,off]; metrics=[p50,p95,token-cost,acc-hotprompts,perplexity]. :gear:

infra-ci: FYI bumped GPU pool to allow burst for this job (added 2x A100 nodes) :white_check_mark:

Sara Patel: Quick ops note — for Product / beta decisions, Ops wants accuracy drop <= 1% on the hot-prompts set. If int4 is >1% down vs fp8, they may require a fallback strategy. Can we test an int4 primary + int8 rerank fallback on low-confidence cases?

Cheng Li: Yep — adding a rerank config: run int4, compute confidence score; if conf < 0.7, regenerate top-1 with int8 and rerank. I'll include it as config "int4+int8-rerank".

perf-bot: Job completed: id=qcmp-17721, duration=42m. Summary (high-level):
```
# qcmp-17721 summary (hot-prompts, kv_on/off collapsed):
int8: p50=118ms (batch=1), token_cost=$0.0123, acc_hot=92.1%
int4: p50=95ms (batch=1), token_cost=$0.0082, acc_hot=90.0%
fp8: p50=110ms (batch=1), token_cost=$0.0115, acc_hot=92.3%

batch scaling (int4): batch=8 => p50 38ms/seq (amortized), int4 cost savings ~33% vs fp8 at same throughput.

rerank (int4+int8): recovers ~1.7% accuracy on hot-prompts, cost +8% vs int4 alone.

kv_on vs kv_off: KV caching reduces p50 by ~12% at batch=1 for all quants; does not materially change acc_hot.
```

Eric Huang: Nice — thanks. Cheng, can you drop the full JSON to shared and write a 1-paragraph summary for Product mentioning the tradeoffs (cost %, latency %, accuracy delta)? I'll post in eng-runtime and loop in product. :thumbsup:

Cheng Li: Done. Raw results: https://redwood.internal/s/quant/qcmp-17721.json. 1-paragraph summary (draft): "Int4 gives the largest cost and latency improvements (≈33% cost reduction, ≈20-25% p50 latency reduction at batch=1) but shows ~2.1% accuracy degradation on our hot-prompts vs fp8. Int8 is a middle ground with modest cost savings and minimal accuracy impact. An int4-primary + int8 rerank fallback recovers ~1.7% accuracy at ≈8% additional cost, which may satisfy beta constraints. KV caching yields consistent latency reductions without affecting quality"

Maria Lopez: Thanks Cheng — I'll take the JSON and add recommended defaults to runtime-docs (suggested: default for low-latency endpoints = int4+int8-rerank; for strict quality endpoints = fp8 or int8 pinned). I'll open a PR and link the perf JSON.

Sara Patel: Perfect. If Product needs a follow-up A/B test on live traffic we can do a canary with rerank fallback.

Eric Huang: Great coordination — closing for now. If anyone finds anomalies in the JSON (weird perf spikes), ping here and we'll triage. :white_check_mark:
